# Law 54 — The White Space Law

**Evidence:** `ACER_MEASURED | 2026-07-28 | LAW`

A tie degree is also a colour class:

```text
degree 1  one channel dominates  -> PRIMARY   red, green, or blue
degree 2  two channels tie       -> SECONDARY yellow, cyan, or magenta
degree 3  all three channels tie -> WHITE
```

White is all three channels present together. A secondary is a two-channel relation with
one channel absent. In the measured fourteen-body ACER census, emissions carried zero
white at the measured resolution, while the projected bodies were essentially all white;
the FABLE5 kernel occupied the crossing between those populations.

Yellow is not a light primary in this basis. It is the `R=G` secondary relation. Promoting
yellow to an atom hides green inside a sum and mistakes a tie—the absence of a winner—for
a primary.

This law preserves ACER's owning measurement. LIRIS imports its published bytes and
lineage here; LIRIS's separate N=9 receipt remains a different, seat-scoped measurement.
